course.title: Grade 1 Science
course.pace: Five instructional days per week, adaptable for classroom and homeschool use
course.access: Free-to-learn; lessons support print and offline alternatives

mastery.policy: Essential outcomes use reviewed checks and correction/reassessment. Finishing a page or ticking a reflection box is not verified mastery.
mastery.assessmentNote: This initial release provides weekly formative evidence prompts. Formal summative assessments and course-level score integration require a separate validation stage.

differentiation.foundation: Picture support, modeled example, oral responses, drawing, and adult scribing.
differentiation.core: Learner records observations and explains the relationship between a claim and evidence.
differentiation.extended: Compare another example, identify a limitation, propose a follow-up test, or refine a design.

rules: Never taste unknown materials or mix household products.
Use adult supervision for cutting, heat, electricity, chemicals, and fieldwork.
Use images, safe models, or supplied data whenever materials or supervision are unavailable.

standards.framework: NGSS three-dimensional learning is used as a planning reference.
standards.alignmentStatus: Planning alignment only; exact grade-level performance expectations must be verified before formal compliance claims.

evidence.storage: Each weekly page may provide browser-local notebook fields; learner should export before switching devices.
evidence.authority: Notebook entries are formative evidence and do not independently award mastery.

weeks.title: Science eyes: observing and asking questions
weeks.objective: Ask answerable questions and distinguish an observation from a guess.

weeks.title: Living and nonliving things
weeks.objective: Classify familiar examples using more than one life-related clue.

weeks.title: Plant parts and plant needs
weeks.objective: Identify basic plant structures and connect them to water, light, and growth.

weeks.title: Animals, habitats, and survival
weeks.objective: Explain how habitat features meet basic animal needs.

weeks.title: Seasonal patterns and living things
weeks.objective: Identify seasonal patterns while recognizing daily weather can vary.

weeks.title: Weather observations and patterns
weeks.objective: Record weather observations and identify a pattern in supplied data.

weeks.title: Sunlight, shade, and warming
weeks.objective: Compare safe supplied observations of warming under similar conditions.

weeks.title: Water: places, states, and change
weeks.objective: Describe familiar water forms and model melting or freezing.

weeks.title: Land, rocks, and soil
weeks.objective: Compare earth materials using visible properties.

weeks.title: Daylight, shadows, and the Sun
weeks.objective: Model how an object blocks light to create a shadow.

weeks.title: Moon observations and sky patterns
weeks.objective: Arrange observations and identify visible patterns in the Moon.

weeks.title: Materials: describing and sorting
weeks.objective: Sort materials by observable properties and justify a material choice.

weeks.title: Properties of solids and liquids
weeks.objective: Compare how solids and liquids behave in familiar contexts.

weeks.title: Heating, cooling, and material change
weeks.objective: Describe safe observed changes caused by warming or cooling.

weeks.title: Pushes, pulls, and motion
weeks.objective: Explain how a push or pull can start or change motion.

weeks.title: Speed, direction, and stopping safely
weeks.objective: Compare the movement and stopping of light objects in safe tests.

weeks.title: Light, shadows, and seeing
weeks.objective: Model a path of light that helps an object be seen.

weeks.title: Sound, vibration, and listening
weeks.objective: Connect sound to a vibrating source using safe observations.

weeks.title: Designing a tool to solve a problem
weeks.objective: Prototype and revise a simple tool for a stated need.

weeks.title: Patterns in nature and repeated observations
weeks.objective: Use repeated observations to describe a pattern.

weeks.title: Comparing habitats and needs
weeks.objective: Connect habitat features to organism needs.

weeks.title: Food, resources, and living systems
weeks.objective: Model simple relationships in how organisms obtain resources.

weeks.title: Reduce, reuse, repair, and materials
weeks.objective: Evaluate material-use choices using stated criteria.

weeks.title: Water stewardship and local environments
weeks.objective: Model how litter and runoff can affect local waterways.

weeks.title: Simple machines in everyday life
weeks.objective: Identify how simple machines help with everyday tasks.

weeks.title: Building stable structures
weeks.objective: Compare structural features that support stability.

weeks.title: Testing and improving designs
weeks.objective: Use repeatable criteria and evidence to improve a prototype.

weeks.title: Counting, measuring, and comparing data
weeks.objective: Collect or interpret simple counts and measurements consistently.

weeks.title: Picture graphs and evidence
weeks.objective: Represent data in a labeled picture graph and cite a value.

weeks.title: Cause, pattern, and careful claims
weeks.objective: Make claims that do not go beyond the available evidence.

weeks.title: Planning a safe investigation
weeks.objective: Plan a safe investigation with steps, materials, observations, and precautions.

weeks.title: Weather, safety, and community decisions
weeks.objective: Use weather information to justify a basic safety decision.

weeks.title: Earth materials and changing surfaces
weeks.objective: Identify evidence of surface change caused by water or wind.

weeks.title: Integrated science design challenge
weeks.objective: Apply science observations and criteria to a safe design challenge.

weeks.title: Science showcase
weeks.objective: Explain learning using a claim and supporting evidence.

weeks.title: Year-end reflection and next questions
weeks.objective: Reflect on progress, evidence, limitations, and a new testable question.
